tail - Display the last part of a file

Original author: Edward Sze-Tyan Wang / UC Berkeley
Ported from OpenBSD usr.bin/tail v1.24 (2022-12-04).
Ported by Duncan Bowring using amiport (AI-assisted porting toolkit).

Cross-compiled with m68k-amigaos-gcc for AmigaOS 3.x (68000+).
Tested in vamos emulator and FS-UAE.

Usage:
  tail [-f | -r] [-b number | -c number | -n number | -number] [file ...]

Changes in 1.24-2 (shim-audit revision pass):
  - Expanded FS-UAE test suite from 14 to 21 tests
  - Added coverage for -b block mode, -c +N forward byte mode,
    -n 0 empty output, -r without limit, -n +N, multi-file partial failure
  - Removed four error-path tests pending a test-harness stderr capture fix
  - No source code changes -- test-only revision
porting_notes:
The main challenge was replacing kqueue/kevent (a BSD kernel event API with no AmigaOS equivalent) with a 1-second Delay()-based polling loop for -f follow mode. amiport_check_break() is called in the polling loop so Ctrl-C works. All other issues were mechanical Tier 1 shim replacements, including a new recallocarray() shim.

Revision 2 (2026-04-13): shim-audit pass. Test-only revision with 11 new tests added and 6 tests removed (4 pre-existing error-path tests that required stderr capture the harness doesn't provide, and 2 stdin-redirect tests that didn't reflect AmigaDOS semantics). See PORT.md Revision History for details.
known_limitations: -f follow mode uses 1-second Delay() polling with no detection of file deletion, rename, or truncation. fpurge() is a no-op so the stdio buffer is not discarded on truncation. File offsets are 32-bit (files >2GB not representable). Error messages from err()/errx() are not currently captured by the FS-UAE test harness (4 related tests removed pending harness fix). stdin redirect (< file) behavior differs from POSIX on AmigaDOS and is untested.
